title.en: Biography of the Marquis of Rang
title.raw: 《穰侯列傳》 Biography of the Marquis of Rang

sentences.zh: 穰侯魏冉者，秦昭王母宣太后弟也。

translations.literal: Wei Ran, Marquis of Rang, was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xuan, mother of King Zhao of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ran, Marquis of Rang, was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xuan, mother of King Zhao of Qin.

sentences.zh: 其先楚人，姓羋氏。

translations.literal: His ancestors were Chu people of the Mi clan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were Chu people of the Mi clan.

sentences.zh: 秦武王卒，無子，立其弟為昭王。

translations.literal: When King Wu of Qin died without sons, his younger brother was established as King Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Qin died without heirs, his younger brother ascended as King Zhao.

sentences.zh: 昭王母故號為羋八子，及昭王即位，羋八子號為宣太后。

translations.literal: King Zhao's mother was formerly titled Lady Mi the Eighth. When King Zhao ascended the throne, Lady Mi the Eighth was honored as Empress Dowager Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao's mother was formerly known as Lady Mi the Eighth. When King Zhao ascended the throne, Lady Mi the Eighth was elevated to Empress Dowager Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣太后非武王母。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuan was not King Wu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuan was not King Wu's mother.

sentences.zh: 武王母號曰惠文后，先武王死。

translations.literal: King Wu's mother was honored as Empress Huiwen and passed away before King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu's mother was honored as Empress Huiwen and predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 宣太后二弟：其異父長弟曰穰侯，姓魏氏，名冉；

translations.literal: Xuan Empress Dowager two younger brothers: different father elder brother called Marquis of Rang, surname Wei clan, named Ran;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuan had two younger brothers: her elder half-brother from a different father was called Marquis of Rang, surnamed Wei, named Ran;

sentences.zh: 同父弟曰羋戎，為華陽君。

translations.literal: her younger full brother was Mi Rong, who served as Lord of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger uterine brother was Mi Rong, who became Lord of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 而昭王同母弟曰高陵君、涇陽君。

translations.literal: King Zhao's full younger brothers were titled Lord of Gaoling and Lord of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao's uterine younger brothers were titled Lord of Gaoling and Lord of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 而魏冉最賢，自惠王、武王時任職用事。

translations.literal: Wei Ran was the most capable of them. He held office and managed affairs from the time of King Hui and King Wu onward.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ran was the most capable among them. He held office and conducted affairs since the reigns of King Hui and King Wu.

sentences.zh: 武王卒，諸弟爭立，唯魏冉力為能立昭王。

translations.literal: When King Wu died, his younger brothers contended for the throne. Only Wei Ran exerted his strength to establish King Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu died, his younger brothers vied for the throne. Only Wei Ran wielded sufficient power to establish King Zhao.

sentences.zh: 昭王即位，以冉為將軍，衛咸陽。

translations.literal: When King Zhao ascended the throne, he appointed Ran as general to guard Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When King Zhao ascended the throne, he appointed Ran as general to defend Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 誅季君之亂，而逐武王后出之魏，昭王諸兄弟不善者皆滅之，威振秦國。

translations.literal: He executed the rebellion of Ji Jun, expelled King Wu's empress to Wei, and exterminated all of King Zhao's disloyal brothers. His might shook the state of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Ji Jun's rebellion, banished King Wu's empress to Wei, and eliminated all of King Zhao's disloyal brothers. His authority shook the state of Qin.

sentences.zh: 昭王少，宣太后自治，任魏冉為政。

translations.literal: Since King Zhao was young, Empress Dowager Xuan governed personally and employed Wei Ran to conduct political affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since King Zhao was young, Empress Dowager Xuan ruled personally and entrusted Wei Ran with conducting political affairs.

sentences.zh: 昭王七年，樗里子死，而使涇陽君質於齊。

translations.literal: In King Zhao's seventh year, Shu Lizi died, and Lord Jingyang was sent as hostage to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of King Zhao, Shu Lizi died, and Lord Jingyang was dispatched as hostage to Qi.

sentences.zh: 趙人樓緩來相秦，趙不利，乃使仇液之秦，請以魏冉為秦相。

translations.literal: The Zhao man Lou Huan came to serve as chancellor of Qin. This disadvantaged Zhao, so they sent Qiu Ye to Qin to request that Wei Ran be made chancellor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao man Lou Huan came to serve as chancellor of Qin. This disadvantaged Zhao, so they dispatched Qiu Ye to Qin to petition for Wei Ran to become chancellor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 仇液將行，其客宋公謂液曰：「秦不聽公，樓緩必怨公。

translations.literal: Qiu Ye about go, his guest Song Gong told Ye: Qin not listen jun, Lou Huan certainly resent jun.
translations.idiomatic: As Qiu Ye was about to depart, his guest Song Gong advised him, "If Qin does not listen to you, Lou Huan will certainly resent you.

sentences.zh: 公不若謂樓緩曰『請為公毋急秦』。

translations.literal: Jun not as tell Lou Huan: please for jun not hurry Qin.
translations.idiomatic: You should tell Lou Huan: 'Please do not hurry Qin on my behalf.'

sentences.zh: 秦王見趙請相魏冉之不急，且不聽公。

translations.literal: The King of Qin will see that Zhao's request to appoint Wei Ran as chancellor is not urgent, and moreover will not listen to you.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin will see that Zhao's petition to appoint Wei Ran as chancellor is not pressing, and moreover will not heed you.

sentences.zh: 公言而事不成，以德樓子；

translations.literal: If you speak and the matter does not succeed, Lou Huan will be grateful to you;
translations.idiomatic: If you speak and the matter does not succeed, Lou Huan will be grateful to you;

sentences.zh: 事成，魏冉故德公矣。」

translations.literal: When affairs are complete, Wei Ran originally had merit in you.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs succeed, Wei Ran will owe you a debt of gratitude.'

sentences.zh: 於是仇液從之。

translations.literal: Then Qiu Ye went along with the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qiu Ye complied.

sentences.zh: 而秦果免樓緩而魏冉相秦。

translations.literal: Qin indeed dismissed Lou Huan and appointed Wei Ran as chancellor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Qin indeed dismissed Lou Huan and appointed Wei Ran as chancellor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 欲誅呂禮，禮出奔齊。

translations.literal: He wished to execute Lu Li, but Li fled to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to execute Lu Li, but Li fled to Qi.

sentences.zh: 昭王十四年，魏冉舉白起，使代向壽將而攻韓、魏，敗之伊闕，斬首二十四萬，虜魏將公孫喜。

translations.literal: In King Zhao's fourteenth year, Wei Ran recommended Bai Qi to replace Xiang Shou as general and attack Han and Wei, defeating them at Yi Guan, beheading twenty-four thousand, and capturing Wei general Gongsun Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of King Zhao, Wei Ran recommended Bai Qi to replace Xiang Shou as general and attack Han and Wei, defeating them at Yiguan, beheading two hundred and forty thousand, and capturing the Wei general Gongsun Xi.

sentences.zh: 明年，又取楚之宛、葉。

translations.literal: The next year, he attacked and took Wan and Ye from Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, he attacked and seized Chu's Wan and Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏冉謝病免相，以客卿壽燭為相。

translations.literal: Wei Ran claimed illness and resigned as chancellor, recommending his guest Qing Shou Zhu to replace him as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ran pleaded illness and resigned as chancellor, recommending his guest minister Shou Zhu to replace him as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其明年，燭免，復相冉，乃封魏冉於穰，復益封陶，號曰穰侯。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhu was dismissed, and Ran became chancellor again. Then Wei Ran was enfeoffed with Rang, and his fief was increased by Tao, earning him the title Marquis of Rang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Zhu was dismissed and Ran became chancellor once more. Then Wei Ran was enfeoffed with Rang, his fief was further increased by Tao, and he was titled Marquis of Rang.

sentences.zh: 穰侯封四歲，為秦將攻魏。

translations.literal: Four years after being enfeoffed as Marquis of Rang, he served as Qin's general and attacked Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Four years after being enfeoffed as Marquis of Rang, he served as Qin's general and attacked Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏獻河東方四百里。

translations.literal: Wei ceded the land east of the Yellow River, four hundred li square.
translations.idiomatic: Wei surrendered four hundred square li of land east of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 拔魏之河內，取城大小六十餘。

translations.literal: He pulled back Wei's territory north of the Yellow River, taking more than sixty cities, large and small.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Wei's territory north of the Yellow River, taking more than sixty cities of various sizes.

sentences.zh: 昭王十九年，秦稱西帝，齊稱東帝。

translations.literal: In King Zhao's nineteenth year, Qin honored itself as Western Emperor, and Qi as Eastern Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of King Zhao, Qin styled itself Western Emperor, and Qi as Eastern Emperor.

sentences.zh: 月餘，呂禮來，而齊、秦各復歸帝為王。

translations.literal: More than a month later, Lu Li came, and Qi and Qin each returned to being called Wang instead of Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later, Lu Li arrived, and Qi and Qin each reverted from Emperor to King.

sentences.zh: 魏冉復相秦，六歲而免。

translations.literal: Wei Ran became chancellor of Qin again, and was dismissed after six years.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ran became chancellor of Qin once more, serving six years before being dismissed.

sentences.zh: 免二歲，復相秦。

translations.literal: Dismissed two years, again chancellor Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After two years' dismissal, he became chancellor of Qin once more.

sentences.zh: 四歲，而使白起拔楚之郢，秦置南郡。

translations.literal: Four years, made Bai Qi pull Chu Ying, Qin established Nan Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After four years, he dispatched Bai Qi to seize Chu's Ying, and Qin established the Nangun commandery.

sentences.zh: 乃封白起為武安君。

translations.literal: Then Bai Qi was enfeoffed as Lord of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Bai Qi was enfeoffed as Lord of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 白起者，穰侯之所任舉也，相善。

translations.literal: Bai Qi, Marquis of Rang recommended employed, mutually friendly.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi was one whom the Marquis of Rang had recommended and employed; they were on good terms.

sentences.zh: 於是穰侯之富，富於王室。

translations.literal: Then Marquis of Rang wealth, wealth exceeded royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, the Marquis of Rang's wealth surpassed that of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 昭王三十二年，穰侯為相國，將兵攻魏，走芒卯，入北宅，遂圍大梁。

translations.literal: In King Zhao's thirty-second year, the Marquis of Rang, serving as chancellor, led troops to attack Wei, routed them at Mang Mao, entered Bei Zhai, and then surrounded Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of King Zhao, the Marquis of Rang, serving as prime minister, led troops to attack Wei, routed Mang Mao, entered Beizhai, and thereupon besieged Daliang.

sentences.zh: 梁大夫須賈說穰侯曰：「臣聞魏之長吏謂魏王曰：『昔梁惠王伐趙，戰勝三梁，拔邯鄲；

translations.literal: Xu Jia, a grandee of Liang, advised the Marquis of Rang: Your servant has heard Wei's high officials tell the King of Wei: Formerly King Hui of Liang attacked Zhao, won a battle at Sanliang, and captured Handan;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia, a grandee of Liang, advised the Marquis of Rang: "Your servant has heard Wei's high officials tell the King of Wei: 'Formerly King Hui of Liang attacked Zhao, won a battle at Sanliang, and captured Handan;

sentences.zh: 趙氏不割，而邯鄲復歸。

translations.literal: The Zhao clan did not cede land, and Handan returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao clan did not cede land, and Handan returned to them.

sentences.zh: 齊人攻衛，拔故國，殺子良；

translations.literal: Qi attacked Wei, captured Guguo, and killed Ziliang;
translations.idiomatic: Qi attacked Wei, captured Guguo, and killed Ziliang;

sentences.zh: 衛人不割，而故地復反。

translations.literal: The people of Wei did not cede land, and the former territory was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei did not cede land, and the former territory was returned.

sentences.zh: 衛、趙之所以國全兵勁而地不并於諸侯者，以其能忍難而重出地也。

translations.literal: Wei and Zhao survive as complete states with strong troops and unannexed lands among the feudal lords because they are able to endure hardship and make heavy territorial concessions.
translations.idiomatic: The reason Wei and Zhao survive as intact states with vigorous armies and lands not annexed by the feudal lords is that they are able to endure hardship and cede territory generously.

sentences.zh: 宋、中山數伐割地，而國隨以亡。

translations.literal: Song and Zhongshan were attacked several times for ceding land, and their states followed them into extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Zhongshan were repeatedly attacked for ceding land, and their states perished in consequence.

sentences.zh: 臣以為衛、趙可法，而宋、中山可為戒也。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks Wei and Zhao can be models, while Song and Zhongshan serve as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers Wei and Zhao worthy of emulation, while Song and Zhongshan serve as cautionary examples.

sentences.zh: 秦，貪戾之國也，而毋親。

translations.literal: Qin is a greedy and violent state with no kin.
translations.idiomatic: Qin is a rapacious and violent state with no kin relations.

sentences.zh: 蠶食魏氏，又盡晉國，戰勝暴子，割八縣，地未畢入，兵復出矣。

translations.literal: Qin nibbles away at the Wei clan and exhausts the state of Jin. Though Wei defeated Baozi and ceded eight counties, the land had not yet been fully handed over before Qin's troops came out again.
translations.idiomatic: Qin nibbles away at the Wei clan and exhausts the state of Jin. Though Wei defeated Baozi and ceded eight counties, the land had not yet been fully handed over before Qin's troops came out again.

sentences.zh: 夫秦何厭之有哉！

translations.literal: How could Qin ever be satisfied!
translations.idiomatic: How could Qin ever be satisfied!

sentences.zh: 今又走芒卯，入北宅，此非敢攻梁也，且劫王以求多割地。

translations.literal: Now again routed Mang Mao, entered Bei Zhai, this not dare attack Liang, moreover coerce wang seek much cede land.
translations.idiomatic: Now it has routed Mang Mao once more and entered Beizhai—this is not daring to attack Liang, but rather coercing the king to cede much land.

sentences.zh: 王必勿聽也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not listen to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not listen to Qin.

sentences.zh: 今王背楚、趙而講秦，楚、趙怒而去王，與王爭事秦，秦必受之。

translations.literal: Now wang back Chu Zhao discuss Qin, Chu Zhao angry depart wang, with wang contend serve Qin, Qin certainly accept.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now abandons Chu and Zhao to negotiate with Qin, Chu and Zhao will grow angry and desert Your Majesty, contending with you to serve Qin, and Qin will certainly accept them.

sentences.zh: 秦挾楚、趙之兵以復攻梁，則國求無亡不可得也。

translations.literal: Qin grasp Chu Zhao troops again attack Liang, then state seek not perish impossible obtain.
translations.idiomatic: If Qin seizes Chu and Zhao's troops to attack Liang once more, then even if our state seeks to avoid destruction, it will not be possible.

sentences.zh: 願王之必無講也。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will absolutely not negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will absolutely not negotiate.

sentences.zh: 王若欲講，少割而有質；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to negotiate, cede little and take hostages;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to negotiate, cede little and take hostages;

sentences.zh: 不然，必見欺。』

translations.literal: not so, certainly see deceived.
translations.idiomatic: If not, you will certainly be deceived.

sentences.zh: 此臣之所聞於魏也，願君［王］之以是慮事也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard this from Wei and wishes you to consider affairs accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: This is what your servant has heard from Wei. I wish you to consider affairs accordingly.

sentences.zh: 《周書》曰『惟命不于常』，此言幸之不可數也。

translations.literal: The Zhou Book says, 'The mandate is not constant'; this means that one cannot count on good fortune again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Book says, 'The mandate is not constant'; this means that one cannot count on good fortune again and again.

sentences.zh: 夫戰勝暴子，割八縣，此非兵力之精也，又非計之工也，天幸為多矣。

translations.literal: Defeating Baozi in battle and obtaining the cession of eight counties was not due to refined military strength, nor to excellent planning; Heaven's favor had much to do with it.
translations.idiomatic: Defeating Baozi in battle and obtaining the cession of eight counties was not due to refined military strength, nor to excellent planning; Heaven's favor had much to do with it.

sentences.zh: 今又走芒卯，入北宅，以攻大梁，是以天幸自為常也。

translations.literal: Now to rout Mang Mao again, enter Bei Zhai, and attack Daliang - this takes Heaven's good fortune as a constant.
translations.idiomatic: Now to rout Mang Mao once more, enter Beizhai, and attack Daliang—this takes heaven's favor as a constant.

sentences.zh: 智者不然。

translations.literal: Wise not so.
translations.idiomatic: The wise do not act thus.

sentences.zh: 臣聞魏氏悉其百縣勝甲以上戍大梁，臣以為不下三十萬。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Wei clan has mobilized all the best armored troops from its hundred counties and above to garrison Daliang. Your servant thinks they number not less than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the Wei clan has mobilized the best armored troops from all its hundred counties to garrison Daliang. Your servant thinks they number not less than three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 以三十萬之眾守梁七仞之城，臣以為湯、武復生，不易攻也。

translations.literal: To guard Liang's seven-ren-high city with three hundred thousand troops—your servant thinks that even if Tang and Wu were revived, they would not easily attack it.
translations.idiomatic: To defend Liang's seven-ren-high walls with three hundred thousand troops—your servant thinks that even if Tang and Wu were revived, they would not easily attack it.

sentences.zh: 夫輕背楚、趙之兵，陵七仞之城，戰三十萬之眾，而志必舉之，臣以為自天地始分以至于今，未嘗有者也。

translations.literal: To lightly turn one's back on Chu and Zhao's troops, scale seven-ren walls, battle a force of three hundred thousand, and be determined to take the city: your servant thinks that from the first division of Heaven and Earth until now, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: To lightly turn one's back on Chu and Zhao's troops, scale seven-ren walls, battle a force of three hundred thousand, and be determined to take the city: your servant thinks that from the first division of Heaven and Earth until now, there has never been such a thing.

sentences.zh: 攻而不拔，秦兵必罷，陶邑必亡，則前功必棄矣。

translations.literal: Attack not pull, Qin troops certainly tired, Tao city certainly perish, then previous merit certainly abandon.
translations.idiomatic: If the attack fails to capture it, Qin troops will certainly be exhausted, Tao city will certainly perish, and then all previous merits will certainly be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今魏氏方疑，可以少割收也。

translations.literal: Now the Wei clan is just wavering; it can be won over with a small concession.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Wei clan is just wavering; it can be won over with a small concession.

sentences.zh: 願君逮楚、趙之兵未至於梁，亟以少割收魏。

translations.literal: I wish you to hasten and make a small concession to gather Wei before Chu and Zhao's troops arrive at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: I wish my lord to hasten and make a small territorial concession to win over Wei before Chu and Zhao's troops arrive at Liang.

sentences.zh: 魏方疑而得以少割為利，必欲之，則君得所欲矣。

translations.literal: Wei is just wavering, and if it can gain advantage from a small concession, it will certainly desire this; then my lord will obtain what he wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei is just wavering, and if it can gain advantage from a small concession, it will certainly desire this; then my lord will obtain what he wishes.

sentences.zh: 楚、趙怒於魏之先己也，必爭事秦，從以此散，而君後擇焉。

translations.literal: Chu and Zhao will be angry that Wei preceded them and will certainly vie to serve Qin. The alliance will thereby scatter, and my lord can afterward choose among them.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Zhao will be angry that Wei preceded them and will certainly vie to serve Qin. The alliance will thereby scatter, and my lord can afterward choose among them.

sentences.zh: 且君之得地豈必以兵哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, jun obtain land how must with troops!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, must my lord's acquisition of land necessarily be through troops!

sentences.zh: 邦晉國，秦兵不攻，而魏必效絳安邑。

translations.literal: If you stabilize the state of Jin without Qin troops attacking, Wei will certainly cede Jiang and Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: If you stabilize the state of Jin without Qin troops attacking, Wei will certainly cede Jiang and Anyi.

sentences.zh: 又為陶開兩道，幾盡故宋，衛必效單父。

translations.literal: You will also open two roads for Tao and nearly exhaust the former Song territories; Wei will certainly cede Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: You will also open two roads for Tao and nearly exhaust the former Song territories; Wei will certainly cede Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 秦兵可全，而君制之，何索而不得，何為而不成！

translations.literal: Qin troops can complete, jun control it, what seek not obtain, what do not complete!
translations.idiomatic: Qin troops can be preserved whole while my lord controls them—what is there to seek that cannot be obtained, what to do that cannot be accomplished!

sentences.zh: 願君熟慮之而無行危。」

translations.literal: Wish jun carefully consider not do danger.
translations.idiomatic: I wish my lord to deliberate carefully and not pursue danger.'

sentences.zh: 穰侯曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Marquis of Rang said: Good.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Rang declared: 'Excellent.'

sentences.zh: 乃罷梁圍。

translations.literal: Then stopped Liang siege.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he lifted the siege of Liang.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏背秦，與齊從親。

translations.literal: Next year, Wei betrayed Qin, with Qi form close alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Wei betrayed Qin and formed close ties with Qi.

sentences.zh: 秦使穰侯伐魏，斬首四萬，走魏將暴鳶，得魏三縣。

translations.literal: Qin made Marquis of Rang attack Wei, beheaded four thousand, routed Wei general Bao Yuan, obtained Wei three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Qin dispatched the Marquis of Rang to attack Wei, beheading forty thousand, routing the Wei general Bao Yuan, and seizing three Wei counties.

sentences.zh: 穰侯益封。

translations.literal: Marquis of Rang moreover increased enfeoff.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Rang's fief was further increased.

sentences.zh: 明年，穰侯與白起客卿胡陽復攻趙、韓、魏，破芒卯於華陽下，斬首十萬，取魏之卷、蔡陽、長社，趙氏觀津。

translations.literal: Next year, Marquis of Rang with Bai Qi guest qing Hu Yang again attacked Zhao Han Wei, broke Mang Mao Hua Yang below, beheaded ten thousand, took Wei Juan, Cai Yang, Chang She, Zhao Guan Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the Marquis of Rang together with Bai Qi and guest minister Hu Yang again attacked Zhao, Han, and Wei, defeating Mang Mao below Huayang, beheading one hundred thousand, and seizing Wei's Juan, Caiyang, and Changshe, as well as Zhao's Guanjin.

sentences.zh: 且與趙觀津，益趙以兵，伐齊。

translations.literal: Moreover, with Zhao Guan Jin, increased Zhao with troops, attacked Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he returned Guanjin to Zhao, augmented Zhao with troops, and attacked Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊襄王懼，使蘇代為齊陰遺穰侯書曰：「臣聞往來者言曰『秦將益趙甲四萬以伐齊』，臣竊必之敝邑之王曰『秦王明而熟於計，穰侯智而習於事，必不益趙甲四萬以伐齊』。

translations.literal: King Xiang of Qi grew fearful and had Su Dai secretly send a letter to the Marquis of Rang on Qi's behalf: Your servant has heard travelers say, "Qin will add forty thousand armored troops to Zhao to attack Qi." Your servant privately assured the king of my humble state: "The King of Qin is clear-headed and skilled in planning, and the Marquis of Rang is intelligent and experienced in affairs; they will certainly not add forty thousand armored troops to Zhao to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang of Qi grew fearful and had Su Dai secretly send a letter to the Marquis of Rang on Qi's behalf: 'Your servant has heard travelers say, "Qin will add forty thousand armored troops to Zhao to attack Qi." Your servant privately assured the king of my humble state: "The King of Qin is clear-headed and skilled in planning, and the Marquis of Rang is intelligent and experienced in affairs; they will certainly not add forty thousand armored troops to Zhao to attack Qi.

sentences.zh: 是何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 夫三晉之相與也，秦之深讎也。

translations.literal: San Jin mutually with, Qin deep enmity.
translations.idiomatic: The alliance of the Three Jin states is Qin's deepest enmity.

sentences.zh: 百相背也，百相欺也，不為不信，不為無行。

translations.literal: They turn their backs on one another a hundred times and deceive one another a hundred times, but do not regard this as faithlessness or misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: They turn their backs on one another a hundred times and deceive one another a hundred times, yet do not regard this as faithlessness or misconduct.

sentences.zh: 今破齊以肥趙。

translations.literal: Now to break Qi in order to enrich Zhao:
translations.idiomatic: Now to break Qi in order to enrich Zhao:

sentences.zh: 趙，秦之深讎，不利於秦。

translations.literal: Zhao, Qin deep enmity, disadvantage Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao is Qin's deepest enmity; this is disadvantageous to Qin.

sentences.zh: 此一也。

translations.literal: This one.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason.

sentences.zh: 秦之謀者，必曰『破齊，獘晉、楚，而後制晉、楚之勝』。

translations.literal: Qin's strategists will certainly say: 'Destroy Qi, exhaust Jin and Chu, and afterward control Jin and Chu when they are victorious.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin's strategists will certainly say: 'Destroy Qi, exhaust Jin and Chu, and afterward control Jin and Chu when they are victorious.'

sentences.zh: 夫齊，罷國也，以天下攻齊，如以千鈞之弩決潰癕也，必死，安能獘晉、楚？

translations.literal: Qi is an exhausted state. To attack Qi with the whole world is like using a thousand-jun crossbow to burst a festering boil: Qi will certainly die, but how can this exhaust Jin and Chu?
translations.idiomatic: Qi is an exhausted state. To attack Qi with the whole world is like using a thousand-jun crossbow to burst a festering boil: Qi will certainly die, but how can this exhaust Jin and Chu?

sentences.zh: 此二也。

translations.literal: This two.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason.

sentences.zh: 秦少出兵，則晉、楚不信也；

translations.literal: Qin little send troops, then Jin Chu not trust;
translations.idiomatic: If Qin sends few troops, then Jin and Chu will not trust us;

sentences.zh: 多出兵，則晉、楚為制於秦。

translations.literal: If many troops are sent, then Jin and Chu will be controlled by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: If many troops are sent out, then Jin and Chu will be controlled by Qin.

sentences.zh: 齊恐，不走秦，必走晉、楚。

translations.literal: When Qi is afraid, it will not run to Qin; it will certainly run to Jin and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi is afraid, it will not run to Qin; it will certainly run to Jin and Chu.

sentences.zh: 此三也。

translations.literal: This three.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason.

sentences.zh: 秦割齊以啖晉、楚，晉、楚案之以兵，秦反受敵。

translations.literal: Qin would carve up Qi to feed Jin and Chu, while Jin and Chu would press it with troops; Qin would instead receive enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Qin would carve up Qi to feed Jin and Chu, while Jin and Chu would press it with troops; Qin would instead receive enemies.

sentences.zh: 此四也。

translations.literal: This four.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 是晉、楚以秦謀齊，以齊謀秦也，何晉、楚之智而秦、齊之愚？

translations.literal: This means Jin and Chu use Qin to plot against Qi and use Qi to plot against Qin. Why should Jin and Chu be so intelligent, and Qin and Qi so foolish?
translations.idiomatic: This means Jin and Chu use Qin to plot against Qi and use Qi to plot against Qin. Why should Jin and Chu be so intelligent, and Qin and Qi so foolish?

sentences.zh: 此五也。

translations.literal: This five.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth reason.

sentences.zh: 故得安邑以善事之，亦必無患矣。

translations.literal: Therefore, if Qin obtains Anyi and handles matters well, there will certainly be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, if Qin obtains Anyi and handles matters well, there will certainly be no trouble.

sentences.zh: 秦有安邑，韓氏必無上黨矣。

translations.literal: Qin have An Yi, Han clan certainly no Shang Dang.
translations.idiomatic: If Qin has Anyi, the Han clan will certainly lose Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 取天下之腸胃，與出兵而懼其不反也，孰利？

translations.literal: To seize the vital organs of the world, compared with sending troops out and fearing they will not return: which is more advantageous?
translations.idiomatic: To seize the vital organs of the world, compared with sending troops out and fearing they will not return: which is more advantageous?

sentences.zh: 臣故曰秦王明而熟於計，穰侯智而習於事，必不益趙甲四萬以代齊矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant therefore says: The King of Qin is clear-headed and skilled in planning, and the Marquis of Rang is intelligent and experienced in affairs; they will certainly not add forty thousand armored troops to Zhao to attack Qi.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant therefore says: The King of Qin is clear-headed and skilled in planning, and the Marquis of Rang is intelligent and experienced in affairs; they will certainly not add forty thousand armored troops to Zhao to attack Qi.'

sentences.zh: 於是穰侯不行，引兵而歸。

translations.literal: Then Marquis of Rang not go, led troops returned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Marquis of Rang did not proceed but led his troops back.

sentences.zh: 昭王三十六年，相國穰侯言客卿灶，欲伐齊取剛、壽，以廣其陶邑。

translations.literal: Zhao Wang thirty six years, chancellor Marquis of Rang spoke guest qing Zao, wished attack Qi take Gang Shou, broaden his Tao city.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of King Zhao, the chancellor Marquis of Rang recommended his guest minister Zao, desiring to attack Qi and take Gang and Shou to expand his fief at Tao.

sentences.zh: 於是魏人范睢自謂張祿先生，譏穰侯之伐齊，乃越三晉以攻齊也，以此時奸說秦昭王。

translations.literal: Then Wei man Fan Ju self called Zhang Lu mister, mocked Marquis of Rang attack Qi, then cross San Jin attack Qi, with this time craftily advised Qin Zhao Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Wei man Fan Ju called himself Master Zhanglu and ridiculed the Marquis of Rang's attack on Qi, saying it was crossing the Three Jin to attack Qi. At this time he craftily advised King Zhao of Qin.

sentences.zh: 昭王於是用范睢。

translations.literal: Zhao Wang then used Fan Ju.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao thereupon employed Fan Ju.

sentences.zh: 范睢言宣太后專制，穰侯擅權於諸侯，涇陽君、高陵君之屬太侈，富於王室。

translations.literal: Fan Ju spoke Xuan Empress Dowager monopolize power, Marquis of Rang monopolize power feudal lords, Jing Yang Jun Gao Ling Jun kind too extravagant, rich exceed wang house.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ju spoke of Empress Dowager Xuan monopolizing authority, the Marquis of Rang usurping power among the feudal lords, and the likes of Lord Jingyang and Lord Gaoling being too extravagant and wealthier than the royal house.

sentences.zh: 於是秦昭王悟，乃免相國，令涇陽之屬皆出關，就封邑。

translations.literal: Then Qin Zhao Wang enlightened, dismissed chancellor, ordered Jing Yang kind all exit pass, go enfeoff city.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon King Zhao of Qin was enlightened. He dismissed the chancellor and ordered the likes of Jingyang to all leave the passes and go to their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 穰侯出關，輜車千乘有餘。

translations.literal: Marquis of Rang exit pass, baggage chariots thousand ride surplus.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Rang left the pass, he had more than a thousand baggage wagons.

sentences.zh: 穰侯卒於陶，而因葬焉。

translations.literal: Marquis of Rang died Tao, because buried there.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Rang died at Tao and was buried there.

sentences.zh: 秦復收陶為郡。

translations.literal: Qin again collected Tao as commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qin reclaimed Tao as a commandery.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：穰侯，昭王親舅也。

translations.literal: Grand Historian said: Marquis of Rang, Zhao Wang close maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian remarks: The Marquis of Rang was King Zhao's own maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 而秦所以東益地，弱諸侯，嘗稱帝於天下，天下皆西鄉稽首者，穰侯之功也。

translations.literal: Qin so east increase land, weaken feudal lords, once titled emperor world, world all west face bow head, Marquis of Rang merit.
translations.idiomatic: The reason Qin expanded eastward, weakened the feudal lords, once styled itself emperor in the world, and made all under heaven face west and bow their heads—these were the Marquis of Rang's merits.

sentences.zh: 及其貴極富溢，一夫開說，身折勢奪而以憂死，況於羈旅之臣乎！

translations.literal: When he reached the extreme of nobility and overflowing wealth, one man's persuasion opened the way, his person was brought low and his power seized, and he died of worry; how much more so for a minister who is merely a sojourner!
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the peak of nobility and overflowing wealth, one man's persuasion opened the way, his person was brought low and his power seized, and he died of worry. How much more vulnerable is a minister who is merely a sojourner!
